parts.latex: Show that the value of $\angle BOC$ is $105^\circ$.
Find the area of triangle $BOC$ to the nearest square metre.
Show that the value of $\angle AOD$ is $67^\circ$.
Find the perimeter of triangle $AOD$ to the nearest metre.

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} \angle BOC &= 243 - 138 \\ &= 105^\circ \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 73 \times 66 \times \sin 105^\circ \\ &\approx 2327 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Fiona needs to find the width of a lake. From her position she can measure the distance to each side of the lake and the angle between those lines. Which rule would be best for her to use to find the width of the lake?

\exfigure{496_q6_1}

solutions.latex:
Two sides ($a$ and $b$) and the included angle $C$ are known, and the opposite side $c$ is required.

So use the cosine rule:
$$c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$$
So the correct option is A.

solutions.latex:

$$\begin{aligned} TH^2 &= 90^2+110^2-2\times 90\times 110\times\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 30\,100 \\ TH &= 173.49\ldots \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} TL &= 173.49\ldots-60 \\ &= 113.49\ldots \\ &\approx 113.5 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

6660.stem:
A yacht race follows the triangular course shown in the diagram. The course from $P$ to $Q$ is 1.8 km on a true bearing of $058^\circ$. At $Q$ the course changes direction. The course from $Q$ to $R$ is 2.7 km and $\angle PQR = 74^\circ$.

\exfigure{825_q25_1}

parts.latex: What is the bearing of $R$ from $Q$?
Use the cosine rule to determine the distance from $R$ to $P$? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{825_q25_s1}

The north lines at $P$ and $Q$ are parallel. The bearing of $Q$ from $P$ is $058^\circ$, so the bearing of $P$ from $Q$ is
$$058^\circ + 180^\circ = 238^\circ$$
From the diagram, $QR$ is reached by turning a further $74^\circ$ clockwise from $QP$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } R \text{ from } Q &= 238^\circ + 74^\circ \\ &= 312^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{The bearing of } R \text{ from } Q \text{ is } 312^\circ$$

meta.self_check: Figure is not to scale; R lies north-west of Q, 312 is consistent with that.
meta.generated_note: Direction of the 74 degree turn read from the figure (R north-west of Q).
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle PQR$, $PQ = 1.8$, $QR = 2.7$ and $\angle PQR = 74^\circ$. Apply the cosine rule to find $RP$.
$$\begin{aligned} RP^2 &= PQ^2 + QR^2 - 2\times PQ \times QR \cos 74^\circ \\ &= 1.8^2 + 2.7^2 - 2 \times 1.8 \times 2.7 \cos 74^\circ \\ &\approx 7.851 \\ RP &\approx 2.80 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ RP \approx 2.8 \text{ km}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

The arrowheads use the house filled Latex head, which is smaller than the crop's large solid heads; that is the only remaining red (rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 14, 22).

6715.stem:
The diagram below shows the plan for a triangular park $ABC$. Fence posts have been located at points A, B and C. AB is 50 m and BC is 80 m. The bearing of B from A is $040^\circ$ and the bearing of C from B is $125^\circ$.

\exfigure{826_q40_1}

figures.cap: triangle ABC with bearings and north lines

parts.latex: What is the size of angle $\theta$?
What is the true bearing of point A from point B?
Find the area of the park? Answer correct to one decimal place.
Find the length of $AC$? Answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
Angles on a straight line at $B$ and the co-interior angle with the north lines give
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= 360^\circ - (180^\circ - 40^\circ) - 125^\circ \\ &= 95^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing} &= 125^\circ + 95^\circ \\ &= 220^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the bearing of } A \text{ from } B \text{ is } 220^\circ$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula with $\angle B = 95^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 50 \times 80 \times \sin 95^\circ \\ &= 1992.389\ldots \\ &\approx 1992.4 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the area of the park is } 1992.4 \text{ m}^2$$
criteria: Uses the area of a triangle formula with one correct value, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in $\triangle ABC$ with $\angle B = 95^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} AC^2 &= 50^2 + 80^2 - 2 \times 50 \times 80 \times \cos 95^\circ \\ &= 9597.25\ldots \\ AC &= 97.9655\ldots \\ &\approx 98.0 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the length of } AC \text{ is } 98.0 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Uses the cosine rule with one correct value, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $h$ be the perpendicular height. Using the sine ratio in the triangle with hypotenuse $10$:
$$\sin66^\circ=\dfrac{h}{10}$$
$$h=10\sin66^\circ$$
Using the tangent ratio in the other right-angled triangle:
$$\begin{aligned} \tan39^\circ &= \dfrac{h}{x} \\ x &= \dfrac{h}{\tan39^\circ} \\ &= \dfrac{10\sin66^\circ}{\tan39^\circ} \\ &\approx 11.28 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct expression for $x$, or equivalent merit

7404.stem:
A mother bird ($M$) leaves her nest ($O$) and flies on a bearing of $048^\circ$ for 9.5 km. A baby bird ($B$) leaves the same nest and flies due South for 4 km.

\exfigure{250_q32_1}

figures.cap: nest O, bird M on bearing 048, bird B due south

parts.latex: Find the value of $\angle MOB$.
Using the cosine rule, find the distance between the two birds, correct to the nearest kilometre.

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $M$ from $O$ is $048^\circ$, so $OM$ makes an angle of $48^\circ$ with north. $OB$ points due south, which is $180^\circ$ from north.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle MOB &= 180^\circ - 48^\circ \\ &= 132^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.self_check: North line and south line are 180 degrees apart.
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle MOB$ we know two sides, $OM=9.5$ and $OB=4$, and the included angle $\angle MOB=132^\circ$. Use the cosine rule.
$$\begin{aligned} MB^2 &= 9.5^2 + 4^2 - 2\times 9.5\times 4\cos 132^\circ \\ &\approx 157.1 \\ MB &\approx 12.5 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ MB \approx 13 \text{ km (to the nearest km)}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

The crop draws the O-to-N segment heavy; it is redrawn at the house 0.6pt because rule 3 allows nothing heavier for a non-graph line. The arrowhead is the filled house head (rule 4).

figures.cap: triangle with sides 7, 10, a and included angle 41 degrees

parts.latex:
Which calculation could be used to find the value of $a$ in this triangle?

\exfigure{710_q2_1}

solutions.latex:
Two sides ($7$ and $10$) and the included angle ($41^\circ$) are known, and $a$ is the side opposite that angle. Use the cosine rule:
$$a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A$$
Substituting,
$$a^2 = 7^2 + 10^2 - (2\times 7\times 10\times\cos 41^\circ)$$
Option A has a plus sign, and options B and C use right-angled or sine-rule forms that do not apply here, so the answer is option D.

meta.self_check: Cosine rule with included angle opposite a; key D matches.

The scores are below 0.85 only because the scan's strokes are about 4 px thick and the house lines are 0.6pt. Rules 1, 2, 3, 11.
